sections.html: Parotocinclus jumbo is one of the largest species of the genus (maximum size is reported to be around 6-7 cm) and one of the prettiest. It is an algae eater.

South America: Paraiba do Norte and Piranhas rivers in Paraiba State, Canhotinho River in Pernambuco State, a tributary of the Mundau River, flowing near the city of Maceio in Alagoas State, and Salgado River in Ceara State.
Inhabits flat areas of shallow clear waters with low current and sandy and rocky bottom.
Not a well known species but good aquarium husbandry with regular water changes and good oxygen content should suffice.

Readily accepts a mixed and varied diet which includes lettuce, cucumber, courgette (zucchini), tablet foods, flake foods, granular foods, frozen bloodworm, to name but a few. Try also to provide rocks covered with algae or other methods like this for this species as they will feed on this, and also the very small microscopic animals that are found amongst the algae.

There is very obvious sexual dichromatism in this species, which has so far not been reported in the aquarium literature. Males get wonderful shining, blueish-green saddles on the back which are missing in females. In addition, the females are much more plump than the males.

There are some spawning reports on the species. It seems to have a positive effect if a rainy season is simulated, as is done with many Corydoras species. In practice this means large water changes with cooler and softer water than the water used for regular keeping. However, the temperature difference should not be too big; about 5°C is suitable.

The fish does not practise brood care in any way. The eggs are sticky and become attached to the glass or tank equipment – again there are many parallels to Corydoras. It is reported that raising the spawn is rather difficult and that the eggs tend to get fungus.
Lexicon: Parotocinclus: ancient Greek, means "alike Otocinclus"; Otocinclus is another genus of catfish. jumbo: refers to the unusual size of the species compared with other members of the genus.

The genus Parotocinclus can readily be distinguished from Otocinclus by the presence of an adipose fin, whereas Otocinclus do not possess one. Dorsal soft rays (total): 8; anal soft rays: 6.

Etymology: the specific name jumbo pertains to the larger size and girth of this Parotocinclus species compared with the rest of the genus.

IUCN Red List: Parotocinclus jumbo is distributed in coastal rivers of the Northeast and the lower São Francisco River, being frequent and abundant. Although subject to impact caused by illegal ornamental fishing, this was not considered a significant threat to the species, therefore it was categorised as Least Concern (LC). Increased monitoring and enforcement of this illegal capture is recommended, since increased fishing pressure could affect Parotocinclus jumbo in a more concerning way (IUCN 2022).
